| `ops-enforcement-trio/*.json` (9 configs) | Spent 2026-08-24, `--no-approval` disclosed. **Reason:** the owner approved this work in session ("gate first, then widen") and no `code-reviewer` agent was available to produce the `=== REVIEW ===` record the approval gate reads; no review record was self-issued, and the absence of an independent verdict is stated in the plan rather than papered over. Job 4 of handoff 9, and **the order matters more than the diff**: the differential gate landed and was proven against a real baseline BEFORE the widening was written, the widening then **failed the gate on all ten paths as undisclosed**, and each was disclosed with its reason. `scripts/check-fileguard-differential.py` is the repo's third "no change may turn a REJECT into an ALLOW" gate — the file-guard classifier had none, and its first widening was the one being proposed. It runs the shell classifier as a subprocess on both sides and compares CATEGORIES, so a reclassification is visible and not just an exit code. **Its first run SKIPPED, and that is the finding worth carrying forward:** at `origin/main` there is no `.claude/hooks/file-guard.sh` because batch 1 PROMOTED it out of `templates/hooks/`, so `git show <baseline>:<path>` failed and the gate returned 0. A renamed subject is not an absent one, and a gate that skips passes forever — the fifth instance of that class recorded here in a month. Fixed with `LEGACY_GUARD_PATHS`. Also: `file-guard.sh` gained an allowlist ahead of the denylist (stem and path-component matching, never substring — `public.pem` freed, `publickeys.pem` not; `tests/fixtures/test.pem` freed, `latest.pem` not), `ExecutionLock.release()` stopped unlinking the lock file (the unlink WAS the race it looked like it prevented), and `config.schema.json`'s "195+ patterns" became an honest description with no count at all, plus `check-comment-replacement` labelled shipped-but-not-wired. **Two plan predictions were wrong and running them is what showed it:** `file-guard.sh` does not source `lib.sh` (self-contained, so the temp-dir extraction needed no companion), and the "wired into nothing" claim in the BACKLOG was already false for two of its three named hooks. Plan: `plan-enforcement-trio.md`. |
| `ops-command-bash-parse-gate.json` | Spent 2026-08-24, `--no-approval` disclosed (owner approved "land it"; no reviewer agent available, no record self-issued). Job 5 of handoff 9. 682 lines of bash across 27 `.claude/commands/*.md` files were never linted — CI's `shellcheck` covers `install.sh` and `.claude/hooks/*.sh` only. Fails on `SC1072`/`SC1073`/`SC1009` **only**, so it is satisfiable the day it lands, and maps shellcheck's line numbers back to `file.md:LINE`. Re-proven against the shipped corpus at execution: `if [ <N> -gt 3 ]; then` inserted at `adapt.md:38` fails with `adapt.md:38: SC1009/SC1073/SC1072`; restored, 7 pass. **The near-miss is the lesson:** the first hand-run targeted `ship.md` and reported GREEN — `ship.md` has ZERO ```bash fences, so the mutation never landed in a linted region, and a `grep` caught it rather than the gate. The in-suite mutation test therefore builds its own fixture, where the mutation cannot fail to land. Honest limit, stated in the plan: this catches bash that does not PARSE, not bash that parses and is wrong. Plan: `plan-command-bash-parse-gate.md`. |
| `ops-hook-log-dedup/*.json` (3 configs) | Spent 2026-08-24, `--no-approval` disclosed (owner approved **item 3 only**; no reviewer agent available, no record self-issued). Job 6 of handoff 9, deliberately scoped DOWN from what was asked: only the three hooks that set a **cwd-relative** `LOG=".claude/hooks/hooks.log"` — `format-typecheck`, `security-reminder`, `session-start` — now source `lib.sh`, set `LOG_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/hooks.log"` and delegate to `hlog`. Run from anywhere but the repo root their log lines landed in another tree or nowhere, silently (finding F107's third form; `command-log-audit.sh`'s `AUDIT_LOG` is the same class, still open as F55). The other 11 local `log()` definitions were left alone: they work, and delegating them means adding `. lib.sh` to 12 more hooks, widening that file's blast radius from 11 to 23 across 16 downstream repos with no defect behind it. Measured before proposing: 14 definitions, **7 distinct bodies, 4 behavioural families** — the handoff's "four implementations" is right at the family level only. Collision audit ran first and came back clean. **My first behavioural test was vacuous and the mutation proof is what exposed it:** restoring the local `log()` failed only the two structural assertions, because the old code appended with `2>/dev/null` and, with no `.claude/hooks/` directory in the foreign cwd, the write failed silently — making "no stray log" trivially true. The fixture now creates that directory on purpose and the same mutation fails three tests. Plan: `plan-hook-log-dedup.md`. |
